# Title
#   Study_Name: Salzer and Kipfmueller 2005 Southern Colorado Plateau Temperature and Precipitation Reconstructions
#-------------------
# Investigators
#   Investigators: Salzer, M.W.; Kipfmueller, K.F.
#-------------------
# Description_Notes_and_Keywords
#   Description: Southern Colorado Plateau multi-millennial tree-ring temperature and precipitation reconstructions.  Three lower forest border tree-ring chronologies were used in the precipitation reconstruction.  Measured ring-width series from construction timbers from archaeological sites are appended to the earlier portions of measured series from living trees at the three sites to substantially lengthen the records.  Upper treeline Bristlecone Pine (P. aristata), whose ring-width variability is a function of temperature, were sampled at timberline in the San Francisco Peaks (~3,536 m).  Increment core and sawed samples were collected from living and dead Bristlecone Pine on both Agassiz Peak and Humphreys Peak.  Long chronologies were constructed by crossdating the deadwood samples with the living tree specimens.  Prior to AD 659 the chronology is composed entirely of deadwood material.  Through conservative standardization techniques and the use of relatively long series, care was taken to preserve low-frequency information in the chronology.  The climate data used in the temperature reconstruction calibration are from the Fort Valley Experimental Research  Station, which is part of the United States Historical Climatology Network.  The station data, from an elevation of 2,239 m and approximately 4.5 km from the high elevation SFP tree-ring sites, span the period 1909-1994.
#-------------------
# Publication
#   Authors: Salzer, M.W. and K.F. Kipfmueller
#   Journal_Name: Climatic Change
#   Published_Title: Reconstructed Temperature and Precipitation on a Millennial Timescale from Tree-Rings in the Southern Colorado Plateau, U.S.A.
#   Published_Date_or_Year: 2005-06-01
#   Volume: 70
#   Issue: 3
#   Pages: 465-487
#   Report_Number: 
#   DOI: 10.1007/s10584-005-5922-3
#   Full_Citation: 
#   Abstract: Two independent calibrated and verified climate reconstructions from ecologically contrasting tree-ring sites in the southern Colorado Plateau, U.S.A. reveal decadal-scale climatic trends during the past two millennia. Combining precisely dated annual mean-maximum temperature and October through July precipitation reconstructions yields an unparalleled record of climatic variability. The approach allows for the identification of thirty extreme wet periods and thirty-five extreme dry periods in the 1,425-year precipitation reconstruction and 30 extreme cool periods and 26 extreme warm periods in 2,262-year temperature reconstruction. In addition, the reconstructions were integrated to identify intervals when conditions were extreme in both climatic variables (cool/dry, cool/wet, warm/dry, warm/wet). Noteworthy in the reconstructions are the post-1976 warm/wet period, unprecedented in the 1,425-year record both in amplitude and duration, anomalous and prolonged late 20th century warmth, that while never exceeded, was nearly equaled in magnitude for brief intervals in the past, and substantial decadal-scale variability within the Medieval Warm Period and Little Ice Age intervals.
